extracted.intended_audience: Program Chairs / conference organizers using OpenReview to configure and run automatic reviewer/area-chair matching
extracted.subtask_description: Creating and running a matching configuration in OpenReview to assign Senior Area Chairs, Area Chairs, and Reviewers to submissions, then reviewing and deploying the proposed assignments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Setup Paper Matching prerequisite
rubrics_metrics.description: In order to run the matching for Senior Area Chairs, Area Chairs, and Reviewers, you must first run Setup Paper Matching from the venue request form.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: After setup, a 'Paper Assignments' link appears on the Program Chair console. This step is required before creating assignment configurations.

rubrics_metrics.name: OpenReview profile requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: All members of a group must have OpenReview profiles in order for the automatic assignment algorithm to run.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If members of your Senior Area Chair, Area Chair or Reviewer group have profiles without publications, you will need to select 'Yes' for 'Allow Zero Score Assignments' or remove members without profiles from the group before running the matcher.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allow Zero Score Assignments
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether or not assignments with scores of 0 should be allowed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a reviewer does not have any publications listed on their profile, they will have an affinity score of 0 with all submissions. Therefore, if you have users without publications, you must select 'yes' to obtain a solution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Create New Assignment Configuration
rubrics_metrics.description: Click the 'New Assignment Configuration' to open a form with default matching settings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You can view, edit or copy values in the form. When satisfied, hit 'Run Matcher' and wait until status is 'Complete'.

rubrics_metrics.name: User Demand
rubrics_metrics.description: The number of users that should be assigned to each paper.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used in the total demand calculation: (number of submissions * user demand) + (number of submissions * alternates).

rubrics_metrics.name: Max Papers
rubrics_metrics.description: The maximum number of papers that can be assigned to each reviewer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to compute max review supply (number of reviewers * max papers) for feasibility checks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Min Papers
rubrics_metrics.description: The minimum number of papers that can be assigned to each reviewer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to compute min review supply (number of reviewers * min papers) for feasibility checks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alternates
rubrics_metrics.description: How many alternate reviewers should be saved per paper.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Alternates are included in the total demand calculation and affect feasibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Paper Invitation
rubrics_metrics.description: Invitation of the submissions that will be assigned in this matching.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defaults to venue_id/-/Submission for single blind and venue_id/-/Blind_Submission for double blind venues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Match Group
rubrics_metrics.description: The group ID of users to be assigned to submissions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Typically the reviewer or area-chair group for the venue; must correspond to users with OpenReview profiles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scores Specification
rubrics_metrics.description: JSON providing further details and customization to scores. Each key represents an edge invitation (affinity score, bid, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fields: 'Weight' to weight a given score value; 'Default' numeric value used when there is not an edge for a reviewer-paper pair; 'translate_map' to map an edge label value into a number. Example aggregate: weight * (affinity score) + weight * (translate_map(bid)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Conflicts Invitation
rubrics_metrics.description: Invitation for storing conflicts between users and papers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defaults to venue_id/user_group/-/Conflict. Conflicts edges feed into the matching to prevent assignments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Custom User Demand Invitation
rubrics_metrics.description: Invitation for edges specifying that certain papers require a custom number of assigned users.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Program Chairs can create edges determining these requests and provide the invitation here. Defaults to venue_id/user_group/-/Custom_User_Demands.

rubrics_metrics.name: Custom Max Papers Invitation
rubrics_metrics.description: Invitation for edges indicating some reviewers request a certain maximum number of assigned papers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The matcher will convert those requests into edges. Defaults to venue_id/user_group/-/Custom_Max_Papers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Solver choice
rubrics_metrics.description: Which algorithm (MinMax, Fairflow, or Randomized) will be used to generate automatic assignments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defaults to MinMax. Choose based on desired optimization behavior: MinMax optimizes scores while respecting min/max quotas; Fairflow tries to ensure minimum affinity for every match; Randomized generates randomized assignments and selects one that maximizes expected total affinity under probability limits.

rubrics_metrics.name: MinMax solver behavior
rubrics_metrics.description: MinMax: Optimizes the scores while respecting the min and max quotas for each paper and reviewer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Good for maximizing aggregate affinity subject to strict quota constraints.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fairflow solver behavior
rubrics_metrics.description: Fairflow: Tries to make every match have at least some minimum affinity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use when you prefer matches to meet a fairness/minimum-affinity criterion rather than pure aggregate score.

rubrics_metrics.name: Randomized solver behavior
rubrics_metrics.description: Randomized: Generates randomized assignments and selects the assignment that maximizes expected total affinity without breaking the probability limits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use when you want less predictability in outcomes; combine with Randomized Probability Limits to cap per-edge probability of selection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Randomized Probability Limits
rubrics_metrics.description: If you select 'Randomized' for the solver, the probability of each reviewer-paper match being generated in a random assignment is limited to this value.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This makes the outcome of the matching more difficult to predict and constrains the randomized selection process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Run Matcher and completion status
rubrics_metrics.description: After filling out the matching configuration form and hitting submit, hit 'Run Matcher' and wait until its status is 'Complete'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only after status 'Complete' will proposed assignments be available to browse/edit/deploy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Modifying Proposed Assignments
rubrics_metrics.description: Once the Matching algorithm completes, the proposed assignments will be generated with options to browse them, view statistics or deploy proposed assignments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Click 'Browse Assignments' to open the edge browser where you can browse, edit, and create proposed assignments. Be careful before deploying proposed assignments — undoing a deployment is difficult and often requires OpenReview staff intervention during office hours.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deployment requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Completion of this step does not make assignments; it only creates a proposed assignment configuration. Those assignments will need to be deployed before Reviewers or Area Chairs will see them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure you are satisfied with edits/statistics before deploying because undoing deployments is hard.

rubrics_metrics.name: Troubleshooting 'No Solution' — feasibility constraints
rubrics_metrics.description: If you get 'No Solution' after running the matcher, view the configuration to see the entire error message indicating infeasible constraints.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example error: 'Total demand (150) is out of range when min review supply is (34) and max review supply is (100)'. This means your constraints require more reviewers or area chairs than you have.

rubrics_metrics.name: Total demand and supply formulas
rubrics_metrics.description: Total demand is equal to (number of submissions * user demand) + (number of submissions * alternates). The max review supply is the number of reviewers available * max papers and the review supply is the number of reviewers available * min papers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Your total demand must fall within the range [min review supply, max review supply] in order to obtain a solution.
